extracted.intended_audience: Putnam Competition supervisors at participating institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed, year-specific instructions for supervisors to administer the 86th William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition (Dec 6, 2025), including eligibility checks, secure printing, in-room procedures, and post-competition scanning and upload of student solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition schedule and problem distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Putnam Competition consists of session A and session B on Dec. 6, 2025; problems will be distributed electronically to supervisors via the Putnam portal on Dec. 6 at 8:00 a.m. EST. Session start/end times vary by time zone (listed in chart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download the problems after 8:00 a.m. EST via the Putnam portal and follow the stated local session start times for signaling the beginning and end of each 3-hour session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition open only to actively enrolled undergraduate students who have not yet received a bachelor's degree; no student may participate more than four times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors must confirm the eligibility of each participant who registers at their institution by approving them at the Putnam portal after they register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student registration and PIN issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must register online before the exam begins to receive their Putnam Identification Number (PIN) and cover sheets. Supervisors have a unique student registration link in their Putnam portal that associates students with the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no deadline for registration, but registration must be completed before the exam begins. If a student's cover sheet is not printed due to last-minute registration, allow them to complete the exam and add the cover sheet later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure printing and handling of problem sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Print the two single sheets of problems for each participant (one for Session A, one for Session B) in a secure environment and place them immediately into envelopes with Session A and Session B problems separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep printed problem sheets in a secure location to ensure problems remain secure until the exam begins; in particular, session B problems must remain secure until the afternoon session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheets: download, distribution, and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Download and print all cover sheets for each participant from the Putnam portal and distribute them to participants, who will cover each of their solutions with the corresponding cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When collecting work, place the appropriate cover sheet in front of each solution to be graded. If a participant does not submit a solution to a problem, discard the corresponding cover sheet (do not scan it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper requirements for submitted solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plenty of unlined clean white 8.5-by-11 inch paper for each student; all submitted solutions must be written on this paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, distribute special Putnam solution paper (an image is available on the Putnam portal to duplicate). Do not accept paper not provided by the supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header format required on each submitted page
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page submitted for grading must include the student's PIN, the problem number (letter A or B followed by a number 1–6), and the page number in the format 'Page k of n' (where n is the total pages for that problem and 1 ≤ k ≤ n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example header layout shown in instructions; ensure students follow the exact format and write the header at the top of each page they want graded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page ordering and scanning dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: When participants hand in work, pages must be in order so the cover sheet for each submitted solution appears on top of the corresponding solution; scan order dictates which pages are submitted for each problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling on solution pages is only a backup. Supervisors must ensure correct order before scanning; discard cover sheets for unattempted problems so they are not scanned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed writing implements and prohibited tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should bring their own writing implements. Pencils or pens with blue or black ink are permitted. Erasers and pencil sharpeners are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other materials such as paper not provided by the supervisor, books, calculators, computers, rulers, or compasses are not permitted in the exam room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile/smart device policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile phones and other smart devices capable of transmitting or receiving information must be turned off and put away during each session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors should announce this at the start of each session and enforce it for the entirety of both sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break policy for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student wishes to take a break during a session and return to the exam room, they must leave behind at their working area all paper and writing implements as well as their cell phone and any smart devices (turned off).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents access to notes or devices while temporarily absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and prohibition of assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must work independently on the problems and may not receive any assistance during the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors may not provide any definitions or clarify any problem statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity on solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are identified by Putnam Identification Numbers (PINs). Participants must not write their name or the name of their institution on their solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure students use only their assigned PIN on solution pages to preserve anonymity in grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Room and proctoring conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should assemble 10 minutes prior to each session. The exam room must be free from noise and other disturbances; the supervisor (or designee) must be present during both sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, a clock should be visible to participants. Arrange seating so no participant can see another's papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required announcements and explicit instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors must make prescribed announcements before each session (e.g., device policy, use only provided paper, do not put solutions to two different problems on same sheet, do not write on reverse side, present all necessary steps and justifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the exact provided script at start and hand-in times to ensure uniform instructions across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start/stop timing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the signal to start work on each session at the indicated time and, after exactly 3 hours, give the signal to stop work on that session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to local session times listed in the guide; supervisors are responsible for precise timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of problem sheets and scrap paper
rubrics_metrics.description: When a session ends, collect the problem sheets and scrap paper; these materials are not to leave the room with the participants (problem sheets may be returned after Monday, Dec. 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no competition materials are taken outside the room during or immediately after the session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of cover sheets and exclusion of scratch/blank pages from scans
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include scratch paper, blank paper, or cover sheets for problems that the student did not attempt in the scanned upload of solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include the cover sheet for each solution actually submitted; discard cover sheets for unattempted problems before scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scanning and PDF file creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scan the submitted solutions to generate a single pdf document for your institution, or several pdfs if file size is unwieldy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanning may be done on Dec. 6, 7, or 8 with office staff under supervision. Recommended filename begins with '2025Putnam' followed by characters identifying your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload deadline and submission via Putnam portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your institution’s solutions by uploading the pdf to the Putnam portal; the deadline for the upload is December 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors must complete the upload by this deadline to ensure inclusion in grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure storage and retention of original solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the original solution papers in your personal possession or in double-lock-and-key secure storage until they are scanned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors must keep originals in secure storage for at least 2 months after the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of graders' scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The scores assigned by the graders are final, and no appeals will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform participants that results will be announced in February 2026 and appeals are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for last-minute registration cover sheet handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If cover sheets have not yet been printed due to last-minute registration, allow the student to complete the exam and add the cover sheets when you have the opportunity to print them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the student's work can still be associated with their PIN and properly covered when scanned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly hand-in and dismissal process
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of each session instruct students to hand in work they wish graded, ensure headers and page ordering are correct, place cover sheets in front of each solution, and do not take any Putnam materials outside the room; then dismiss students (after Session A they may be dismissed for lunch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congratulate students and follow the specified scripted hand-in announcement to maintain uniform procedure.
